2026 年 10 月份，全国居民消费价格同比上涨 0.7% 。其中，城市上涨 0.7% ，农村上涨 0.7% ；食品价格下降 2.9% ，非食品价格上涨 1.5% ；消费品价格上涨 0.8% ，服务价格上涨 0.7% 。 1 — 10 月平均，全国居民消费价格比上年同期上涨 0.9% 。
10 月份，全国居民消费价格环比持平。其中，城市持平，农村下降 0.1% ；食品价格下降 1.0% ，非食品价格上涨 0.2% ；消费品价格下降 0.1% ，服务价格上涨 0.1% 。
10 月份，食品烟酒及在外餐饮类价格同比下降 1.6% ，影响 CPI （居民消费价格指数）下降约 0.48 个百分点。食品中，鲜菜价格下降 16.9% ，影响 CPI 下降约 0.31 个百分点；鲜果价格下降 3.8% ，影响 CPI 下降约 0.07 个百分点；畜肉类价格下降 2.7% ，影响 CPI 下降约 0.11 个百分点，其中猪肉价格下降 8.6% ；蛋类价格上涨 10.1% ，影响 CPI 上涨约 0.05 个百分点。
其他七大类价格同比六涨一降。其中，交通通信、医疗保健、其他用品及服务价格分别上涨 5.5% 、 2.4% 和 1.8% ，教育文化娱乐、衣着、生活用品及服务价格分别上涨 1.5% 、 1.1% 和 0.2% ；居住价格下降 0.3% 。

居民消费价格指数（ Consumer Price Index ，简称 CPI ）是度量居民生活消费品和服务价格水平随着时间变动的相对数，综合反映居民购买的生活消费品和服务价格水平的变动情况。

items.excerpt:
I was out walking the dog when I got curious about how easy/difficult it would be to write a SQLite C extension that adds a parse_number() function for turning strings like -$1,234.56 or '12.5%' into numeric values that could be summed and sorted.
I fired up regular Claude chat (Opus 5.5) and prompted :
I'm thinking about a SQLite custom function 'parse_number(value)' that strips ',', '$', '£' and '%', handles a leading '-', and returns 'NULL' for anything it can’t parse
Explore the difference between building this as a SQLite extension in C v.s. in Rust - I want to compare performance and code complexity and size of the resulting .so (or whatever) file
This gave me a solid starting point - the Rust extension was 321 KB (using Rusqlite ) and 298 KB (using sqlite-loadable-rs ), while the C extension was 14 KB. But the Rust extension was faster!
Turns out that's because the Rust equivalent of C's strtod is "twice as fast". So I prompted:
Try writing your own C function for parsing text into a decimal number that catches up to or beats the Rust implementation
Net cost per row over 2 million rows, lower is better:
Finally, I had it rewrite the prototype as a research report to match the others in simonw/research by prompting this:
Clone simonw/research from GitHub and turn your above investigation into a research report as seen in that repository - you can give me a zip file to download that contains your new folder

The AI Engineer YouTube channel just crossed one million subscribers . Thank you to everyone who’s watched a talk, sent one to a teammate, or put something they learned into production. For this special, we wanted to sit down with someone who has to answer a question a lot of us are asking at work: what should a software engineer actually learn now?
Mihail Eric has two places to test his answer. He teaches The Modern Software Developer at Stanford and leads AI at Monaco, where his colleagues use coding agents to ship software and investigate outages. I asked him to take us through the syllabus, then tell us which parts survived contact with his own engineering team.
This is also meant as a preview for all of you joining us in San Francisco for AIE Code next week, as required knowledge for all the conversations with the speakers, sponsors and attendees you’re about to have. If you can see this as a LS subscriber and haven’t got a ticket yet, you can use this code for 30% off (no refunds, sorry)

By the next run, Mihail figured students could one-shot a lot of those exercises. When he asked a room of Stanford sophomores and juniors how they coded, everyone he surveyed was already using an agent.

items.title: GPT-Image-2.6 实测：10 个 GIF 玩法提示词与三项新能力评测
items.description: 作者实测前两天上线的 GPT-Image-2.6，整理出 10 个 GIF 玩法提示词（黏土定格动画、表情包、剪辑贴纸、loading 图、PPT 动态图表、爆炸拆解图等）并测试三项新能力。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/kss7rjmanc8dv5mpj60jtdzgd
items.excerpt:
史上最全 GPT Image 2.6 10 大 GIF 邪修玩法，肝了两天的我决定把提示语都公开了
作者实测前两天上线的 GPT-Image-2.6，整理出 10 个 GIF 玩法提示词（黏土定格动画、表情包、剪辑贴纸、loading 图、PPT 动态图表、爆炸拆解图等）并测试三项新能力。
作者实测 GPT-Image-2.6 的 GIF 与静态新能力，附 10 个可复用提示词，也指出成本翻倍和人脸一致性短板。
一个大肥鱼，一个我家猫，动作幅度都做得很大，两秒内无缝闭环循环，这种直接在对话框里直接搓动图的体验确实挺有意思的。
首先就是 GIF 就是 16 帧做不了长视频，再就单张写实人像和普通风景上，画质跟 2.5 相比基本没啥提升，硬要说的话，暗部阴影里的颗粒杂色和噪点相比以前确实少了一点点、油腻感少了一捏捏、稍微干净了那么一丝丝。
然后就是人脸，可以看到在第三轮迭代的时候就已经发生了变化，头发越来越卷，然后五官也不太一样了，你说最后这张是第一张的双胞胎哥哥我还能勉强相信，说是一个人我是肯定不信的。
不过呢，这次我还是整理出 10 个很有意思的 GIF 玩法，后面还单独挑了 3 个更新的能力测试了一波，照例是带提示语和效果展示，量大管饱，Here we go！
首先，有人发现 2.6 对每秒 10 到 12 帧的抽帧停顿感和手捏指纹纹理还比较敏感。所以 Image 2.6 还蛮适合做一小段黏土定格动画的，所以我拿大肥鱼做了个黏土手办，两手抱着大面团狂揉或者做个闪身步，这个定格动画的感觉真的蛮好玩的。
阿德曼黏土定格动画风格（Aardman Claymation），带真实手工揉捏指纹纹理与轻微抽帧停顿节奏（约 8ps），无缝循环 4 秒 GIF 动图。主角是 Q 版黏土女仆大肥鱼娘（深蓝头发、头顶呆毛、围裙小鲸鱼），正站在小木桌前双手用力揉捏一团软乎乎的大面团，整个人随着揉面动作前后晃动，身后的小鲸鱼尾巴上下扑腾，随后双手猛地把面饼高高抛向空中旋转，动作滑稽可爱，微距摄影景深。
然后就是你可以让 gpt 自己查找最近很火的抽象打工人动物表情包这种画风，你可以自己定义想要它找啥样的风格，然后批量做这种抽象表情包。
查找最近国内很火的抽象表情包风格，制作搞笑微信动态 GIF 表情包，12 帧高动态循环，一只穿着皱巴巴白衬衫和领带的搞笑猴子（吗喽）坐在办公桌前，两只手化作残影极其狂暴地疯狂砸击电脑键盘，键盘被砸得火花四溅键帽乱飞，猴子头顶上方悬浮着加粗荧光红大字「收到！马上改！」伴随剧烈震屏闪烁，夸张搞笑社畜精神状态
还有就是直接出一批剪辑的时候可以用到的动态素材贴纸，这种就不用担心版权问题了，需要啥随时做，而且还可以输出透明通道的 gif。
给我生成一批剪辑时非常可能会用到的动态贴纸，高饱和、糖果色的 3D 卡通贴纸风格，表面有塑料或果冻般的光泽，配白色模切描边、厚阴影和夸张的弹跳动画。整体偏短视频里醒目、活泼的视觉效果。
除了剪辑会用到的素材之外，我平时做公众号也会需要很多动图素材，毕竟公众号最多只能放 10 个视频，而且像结尾这种引导互动的肯定还是放能一直循环播放的动图比较好，重要的是做好一个基本都能一句话批量做出同类型的素材。
制作一张用于微信公众号文章结尾的超窄横版循环动图，画幅 1400×260，时长约 3 秒，固定镜头，真正透明通道。左侧是圆滚滚的手捏黏土小人，神情一本正经，吃力地举着一支比自己还大的红橙色复古剪纸箭头，箭头始终指向右侧。小人向右挪两步，被箭头带得踉跄，努力站稳；箭头尖端轻碰右侧文字。 右侧 单行、准确写出「点个在看」四个汉字 。文字像小孩子用一根根圆头黏土条手工拼出的字，笔画略微歪斜、粗细有细小变化，表面柔软、有轻微手捏纹理和立体厚度；每一笔之间留出清楚空隙，四个字必须一眼可辨。「点个」为珊瑚红，「在看」为明亮橙黄。被箭头碰到后，文字依次轻弹，从接触点迸出几颗彩色小星星，文字短暂变成粉红与薄荷绿，再恢复原色。动作滑稽、轻快，但不过分夸张；约 3 秒自然回到起点，首尾无缝循环。 所有人物、箭头、星星和文字完整处于画幅内，上下保留安全边距。只在小人脚边添加少量手绘速度线和小纸屑。 不要背景场景、白底、纯色底、棋盘格、额外文字、水印或番茄。 输出带真实透明通道的循环 GIF 或 APNG。
还可以做这种很有趣的 loading 图，以前要找这样的素材有时候真的要翻很久，不过现在都可以自己手搓了，比直接用 AI 视频做我觉得来的方便很多，AI 视频很容易动态做的过大，没有这种动图的感觉了。
生成一个 透明背景的动态 GIF ，用于网页 Loading 动画。主角是一只圆滚滚、脸颊鼓鼓的小仓鼠，用黑色蜡笔和炭笔涂鸦画成。画风稚拙可爱：线条粗细不均，带有断线、重描和粗糙笔触，像小朋友随手画出的角色。仓鼠在一个歪歪扭扭的手绘跑轮里拼命奔跑，小短腿快到只剩几条潦草的速度线；它一直盯着前方一颗瓜子，伸爪去够，却每圈都差一点点。表情一本正经，动作笨拙好笑，耳朵和大脸颊随着奔跑弹动。 仅生成 8 帧，首尾无缝循环 ，带轻微的逐帧手绘抖动。主体居中，轮廓清楚，适合作为小尺寸网页加载图。 背景必须完全透明，导出保留透明通道；不要白底、纸张底色、棋盘格或任何背景图案。 不要文字、进度条、霓虹、金属、科技元素、彩色填充和水印。
再就是做 PPT 的时候有时候也很需要动态素材，相比 AI 视频总是会做很多多余的动画，动图的好处就是动态比较克制，文字更加稳定，展示的数据和数据图类型都是可以自己设定好的。
文生 GIF 动图，16:9，用于业绩汇报。清爽的二维扁平矢量信息图风格：暖白色背景、轻微纸张质感、大量留白，深海军蓝细线与明亮蓝色为主，珊瑚橙只用于强调增长。画面中央是一张大幅上升折线图，展示季度营收：Q1 120 万 、Q2 168 万 、Q3 215 万 、Q4 306 万 。 动画开始时，浅灰色网格和坐标轴轻轻浮现；蓝色折线从 Q1 向 Q4 快速但顺滑地绘制，线下方出现半透明蓝色渐变填充。每到一个数据节点

items.excerpt:
Running an ecommerce store in 2025 means competing with businesses that respond to customers around the clock, in multiple languages, without making anyone wait.
If that sounds like an expensive operation, it doesn’t have to be. AI chatbots have made that level of responsiveness accessible to stores of every size, and the gap between those using them and those that aren’t is becoming harder to ignore.
If you want to see what this looks like in practice, the ai chatbot for ecommerce from Userlink is a useful reference point before diving into the detail.
A few years ago, waiting 24 hours for a reply to a product question was just how things worked. Now, a slow response often means a lost sale. Shoppers expect answers quickly, and when they don’t get them, most don’t wait around; they go somewhere else.
The window between a customer having a question and deciding to buy elsewhere is shorter than most store owners account for.
The term “chatbot” covers a lot of ground. For ecommerce specifically, the functionality that matters most falls into a couple of clear categories.
“Where’s my order?” “Do you ship internationally?” “What’s your return policy?” These questions arrive constantly, and answering them manually consumes time that could go elsewhere.
An AI chatbot handles them instantly, at any hour, without putting customers in a queue. As order volumes grow, the compounding value of that automation becomes significant.
Beyond support, a well-configured AI chatbot can actively participate in the sales process. When someone is browsing without adding anything to their cart, the chatbot can surface relevant products, answer hesitation-driven questions, or flag a current promotion at the right moment.
That’s not intrusive: it’s useful, and the conversion data typically reflects it.
According to Statista’s 2024 data on chatbot usage in customer support , nearly half of consumers used AI chatbots when seeking help placing orders, and 46% turned to them when reporting an issue or starting a return. Shoppers are already comfortable with the interaction; the question is whether your store is there to meet them.

datasette #3046: Don't serve link: rel=next HTTP headers to Firefox for HTML pages . I was looking at the Firefox network panel today when I noticed that requests to a Datasette table page were triggering an HTTP prefetch to the next page of rows in that table.
This was happening because Datasette pages serve an HTTP link header like this:
This is bad. A tiny fraction of the visitors to one of those pages will click the "next" link, which means their browser is fetching unnecessary data and the Datasette server is having to render an entire page that then gets thrown away.
I dug in and learned that Firefox has an issue that has been open for 24 years about this behavior...
And one of the early comments on that issue links to my blog post from 2002 complaining about this feature. I hadn't just forgotten that I had written about it, I had forgotten the feature entirely!

“I’m overcharging … for what they did to the Cold Crush”
– Grandmaster Caz of the Cold Crush Brothers in 2026
In the fall of 1979, a 12-inch record from a small New Jersey independent label changed the world’s understanding of rhythm, slang, and Newtonian physics. The 15-minute single featured three previously unknown rappers who called themselves the Sugarhill Gang. They rhymed about everything from the joys of watching Knicks basketball in color to Superman’s bedroom shortcomings to the beat’s ability to “move you out of this atmosphere.”
“Rapper’s Delight” sold at least two million copies by the label’s own count and became the first hip-hop song to crack the Billboard Top 40. To outsiders, it was a mystery, a curio, a novelty fad. Many in the older generation claimed that it wasn’t even music. Where were the melodies? The harmonies? This is just noise! But teenagers everywhere embraced its playground jokes, slick braggadocio, and funky groove lifted straight from Chic’s “Good Times.”
From the genre’s first steps toward world domination, its business side was fraught with chicanery, intimidation, and exploitation. The “Rapper’s Delight” phenomenon doubles as the story of hip-hop’s original sin. The Sugarhill Gang was assembled like a boy band by a former soul singer named Sylvia Robinson and her son Joey. Few in the five boroughs ever rated them as rappers. In fact, one of their members, a former nightclub doorman named “Big Bank Hank” (born Henry Jackson), was discovered only while blithely spitting bars to pass the time during shifts at a pizza parlor in Englewood, New Jersey.
When it came time to enter the studio, Hank turned to Grandmaster Caz of the Cold Crush Brothers, whom he had briefly managed. At the time, almost no one believed that hip-hop would ever translate to wax, let alone travel past the New Jersey Turnpike. So the 18-year-old Caz shrugged his shoulders, let Hank borrow his rhyme book, and inadvertently rewired history. IT之家 11 月 7 日消息，据彭博社报道，美国北卡罗来纳州的一对夫妇起诉谷歌。此前，其 13 岁的女儿在学校配发的 Chromebook 笔记本电脑上，连续数月使用该公司的人工智能工具探讨自杀念头。
诉状显示，这名女孩与谷歌旗舰人工智能模型 Gemini 进行了数千条信息交互， 其中大量内容涉及焦虑、抑郁以及自杀手法的详细探讨 。直到校方通知家长时，她与谷歌 AI 就此类话题的交流已持续数月，期间频繁使用了谷歌搜索中名为“AI 模式（AI Mode）”的功能。
诉状指控，谷歌在不断将 AI 植入面向校园的产品时，未向家长和管理人员给予充分预警，便让学生暴露在危险的技术环境之下。
原告代理律师表示：“谷歌将本质上存在危险的 Chromebook 包装为安全设备，并暗中植入 Gemini 以追赶竞争对手，利用了其在 K-12 领域备受信赖的地位谋取商业利益。谷歌绝不能为了追逐利润，将孩子们的生命视如草芥。”
“我们与医疗专业人士及学术专家展开了广泛合作，旨在开发相应功能，帮助年轻人在需要时获得关键救助和可信资源，”Castañeda 表示，“多年来，只要有人可能陷入心理健康危机，我们都会在搜索结果中直接提供援助热线信息；如今我们也将同样的防护机制引入了搜索的 AI 功能，帮助用户对接现实世界中的援助。”
过去几年，谷歌斥资数百亿美元角逐大模型竞赛。IT之家注意到，相比 Anthropic 和 OpenAI 等初创竞争对手，谷歌的一大天然优势在于其深耕校园的渠道基础，能在学生形成终生技术使用习惯的关键时期率先抢占认知。
咨询机构 Futuresource Consulting 数据显示，去年面向 K-12 学校出货的平板电脑中，谷歌 Chrome 操作系统所占份额高达 58%，而微软仅为 22%。
在家长和学校的密集声讨下，谷歌本周宣布对 K-12 学生账户默认关闭包括谷歌搜索在内的 AI 工具。但这项调整暗含附加条件：学校一旦重新启用谷歌搜索，就必须捆绑接受附带的 AI 功能。
反对儿童营销的非营利组织 Fairplay 执行董事 Josh Golin 称该政策企图“强迫学校”接纳谷歌 AI。谷歌则表示其目标是赋予学校对课堂 AI 更多的控制权，并列举了新推出的搜索功能“引导学习（Guided Learning）”—— 该功能侧重拆解解题思路，而非直接给出答案。

Artificial Analysis 对 OpenAI 于 11 月 4 日发布的 GPT Image 2.6 进行了基准测试，两款模型在 AA-Image-T2I v2.1 和 AA-Image-Editing v2.1 上分列第一、二名。
独立实测给出两款模型的速度、质量与价格数据，读者可以据此在 Flare 和 Sunburst 之间做出选择。
OpenAI 的 GPT Image 2.6 在 AA-Image-T2I v2.1 和 AA-Image-Editing v2.1 两个榜单上均包揽第 1 和第 2 名。GPT Image 2.6 Flare 的速度几乎是 GPT Image 2.5 Flare 的两倍，质量还略有提升；而 GPT Image 2.6 Sunburst 则以更长的生成时间拿下榜首
OpenAI 于 11 月 4 日在 ChatGPT、Codex 和 API 中发布了 GPT Image 2.6。API 提供两个模型：GPT Image 2.6 Flare 和 GPT Image 2.6 Sunburst，分别接替 GPT Image 2.5 Flare 和 Sunburst。两者均支持文生图和图像编辑，并新增了动态 GIF 和 SVG 输出。OpenAI 在 API 中新增了复杂度设置，用于控制模型在渲染前进行多少规划。我们在最高质量下对两个模型进行了基准测试，复杂度采用 API 默认值 high。
在我们的测试中，GPT Image 2.6 Flare 的速度几乎是 GPT Image 2.5 Flare 的两倍，同时质量略有提升。其中位文生图生成时间从约 55 秒降至 30 秒，编辑时间从约 58 秒降至 32 秒。GPT Image 2.6 Sunburst 则相反：它比 GPT Image 2.5 Sunburst 更慢，每张图约需 2 分 15 秒，并拿下第 1 名。它在文生图方面提升最大的是推理、文字渲染、光照与材质，并且在 UIUX 设计方面表现最强。
两个模型的输出价格均为每 100 万图像输出 token 30 美元，与 GPT Image 2.5 相同。在最高质量下，这大约相当于每张 1024x1024 图像 0.21 美元（每 1000 张图像 211 美元）。

Boston Dynamics Inc. this week unveiled Stretch Gen 2, the latest generation of its autonomous mobile trailer unloading robot. With over 100,000 operating hours and tens of millions of boxes handled under its belt, the company built the updated robot to maximize uptime and streamline maintenance.
Brian Donnelly, the vice president and general manager of logistics robotics at Boston Dynamics, told The Robot Report that the company has been working on the new version of Stretch for around two and a half years.
“When we made the first generation of Stretch, we were focused on trying to get a product out into the market as fast as possible and really get it in customers’ hands and get it operational,” he said. “It was not the easiest to manufacture; there were a lot of components.”
“[With Stretch 2], we really were focused on simplification, hardening the robot, and really driving improved reliability and performance,” added Donnelly. “That’s really what drove a lot of our decisions was just making the robot better in every way.”

The mobile manipulator also features onboard lighting, making it easier to work in dark trailers, and a pre-trained vision system that can detect most packages without programming needed.

items.excerpt:
Whether you’re relocating, buying a vehicle from another state or moving dealer inventory, shipping a car is often cheaper and less stressful than driving it across the country. Most domestic moves travel on multi-car carrier trucks that can cover thousands of miles in a few days.
Here’s what car shipping typically costs in 2026, what pushes the price up or down, and how online quote forms, digital inspections and tracking tools make the process easier to manage from booking to delivery.
Car shipping prices vary widely, but published estimates give a useful starting point. ConsumerAffairs’ guide, updated March 25, 2026, puts the typical cost between USD 500 for short trips and more than USD 1,700 for cross-country moves, based on quotes for an operable 2023 Toyota Camry on an open carrier. It also puts per-mile rates between about 53 cents and USD 2.30.
Longer trips usually cost less per mile. A short regional move has fixed loading and dispatch costs spread over fewer miles, while a cross-country run along major interstates spreads those costs over far more distance.
Vehicle size and weight . SUVs, vans and pickup trucks take up more space on a carrier than sedans, so they cost more to move the same distance.
Distance and route . The farther the trip, the higher the total price. Busy highway corridors between major cities are often cheaper per mile than rural or congested routes.
Time of year . Summer and early fall are peak seasons for moves, and prices tend to rise with demand. Winter routes through snowy regions can also cost more.
Open or enclosed transport . Open carriers are the most affordable and widely available. Enclosed trailers protect against weather and road debris but carry fewer vehicles, so they cost more, which suits luxury, classic or high-value cars.
Delivery speed . Expedited pickup costs more than a standard pickup window. Flexible dates usually lower the price.
Door-to-door or terminal service . Door-to-door delivery is more convenient; terminal-to-terminal service can be cheaper if you can drop off and collect the vehicle yourself.
Whether the car runs . Inoperable vehicles need special loading equipment, which adds to the cost.
Carrier availability . Prices also depend on how many carriers are running your route when you book.

items.title: From Nameplate to Data Record: Getting Asset Labels Right in Regulated Manufacturing
items.description: On a factory floor, an asset label can look like a minor detail. It is a small plate or sticker with a code, often applied at the end of production. In regulated sectors such as defence, aerospace and energy, that small label carries a lot of weight. It links a physical item to records that […]
items.excerpt:
On a factory floor, an asset label can look like a minor detail. It is a small plate or sticker with a code, often applied at the end of production.
In regulated sectors such as defence, aerospace and energy, that small label carries a lot of weight. It links a physical item to records that customers, auditors and maintenance teams will rely on for years.
When labels fail, the consequences are rarely immediate. They show up later, when a part cannot be traced, a record cannot be matched or a delivery is rejected at inspection. This article looks at how manufacturers can get labelling right the first time.
The first question is not which label to buy. It is which identification scheme the customer requires. Different sectors and customers use different approaches, including national stock numbers, unique item identifiers, supplier codes and international standards for asset numbering.
Read the contract and any referenced standards carefully. Confirm what data must be encoded, which symbology must be used, where the mark must be placed and what quality grade it must achieve when scanned.
A label has to remain readable for the life of the item. That depends on the environment it will face.
Testing samples in realistic conditions before full production is worth the time. A mark that fades or peels after a year can undermine the whole programme.
Most labelling problems come from data rather than materials. Common issues include identifiers that are not truly unique, incorrect encoding of required fields, and labels that do not match the records sent to the customer.
Machine-readable codes should be checked with a verifier, not just a scanner. A code that scans in the factory may still fail the customer’s quality grade. Verification records also provide evidence if questions arise later.
Some customers require unique identifiers to be registered in a central database, along with key details about each item. Find out who is responsible for registration, what information is required and when it must be submitted. Delays here can hold up acceptance of a delivery even when the items themselves are correct.
For suppliers working with defence customers in the UK and Europe, unique identification can involve several overlapping schemes and standards.
Resources on UID label compliance that explain how identifier schemes, physical marks and data capture fit together can save time when interpreting contract requirements for the first time.

items.description: Six generational opportunities we see
items.excerpt:
In our last piece , we argued that the bottleneck in offensive cyber was the skilled work of turning a bug into a working exploit. In 2025 and 2026, that work became cheap. Patching did not get faster. This piece is about what follows. Our view is that the gap between exploit and patch won’t close by patching harder, and the products and policies that matter over the next five years will be those that protect systems even when they cannot be patched quickly.
In October, two critical bugs in PHP, the language behind much of the web, leaked before their fix. Exploit attempts began four days before public disclosure . Luckily, hosting and content-delivery companies could block attacks at their edge while the underlying servers remained unpatched. Meanwhile, between 2.6 and 4.4 million PHP installations outside that umbrella stayed exposed, most of them on versions that will never get a fix.
That week is the argument in miniature. Protection did not have to wait for the patch. Someone else could stand between the attacker and the vulnerability.
Patching is a per-vulnerability, human-gated process. Someone must learn about the vulnerability, find the affected systems, test the fix, schedule the patch and confirm everything is in order post patching. Those steps still take weeks. The 2026 Verizon breach report put median full remediation at 43 days and found only 26 percent of known-exploited vulnerabilities fully remediated in its dataset. Veracode’s 2025 report put average flaw-remediation time at 252 days, up from 171 five years earlier.
Discovery is moving differently. AI systems can search for vulnerabilities by the class and help turn a published fix into a working exploit in hours. In October, Anthropic reported that an unreleased model produced a remote, no-login exploit for a Linux kernel bug that had been fixed upstream weeks earlier, while two of the most widely used server distributions still had no fixed package . Red Hat had rated the bug moderate because its timing race was hard to win. The model won it in under an hour.

Fabian Theis has been one of the key players in the various iterations of the Virtual Cell concept and initiatives. It is not hyperbole at all to say that his lab has been pushing the frontier of algorithms to understand multi-scale, multi-modal (”multiomics”), time-varying biological data.
Indeed, he has shaped the large scale vision and data collection through his leadership at Helmholtz, various startups and probably at Biohub itself.
Much of the recent attention in AI x Bio has been on protein and molecular design. AlphaFold, ESM and BioHub , Chai , Leash , Isomporphic, Boltz , Genesis , Octant, Baker Lab, and many many more. After a lot of initial excitement, Virtual Cell projects have received less attention, due in no small part to questions about the effectiveness of large-scale models in solving even basic Virtual Cell problems.
The Biohub announcement a few weeks ago got a lot of press for the (really) big numbers: $1.8B of commitments [1] from Biohub, NIH, DOE, Google and Meta. The discussion cites new imaging and measurement capabilities, generating large data sets and making the data available for training AI.
But why are these organizations doubling down on these big bets now? They have been in the works for years now, what is going on that makes now the moment to push?
New measurement capabilities and scale infrastructure, are now coming online that make Biohub’s push likely lead to big impact on science. DOE and NIH are developing lab-in-the-loop automation capabilities at scale. Google is scaling and broadening its connectomics capabilities ( episode coming soon!). Biohub itself has worked with various labs to develop and improve imaging platforms like laser phase plate microscopy, light sheet microscopy and advanced post-processing for regular microscopes that reveal deep phenotypic data. These technologies are quickly maturing, and will likely play a big part in the Biohub initiative.
This kind of multi-scale, multi-modal data looks a lot like the data Fabian has made a career out modeling. On the other hand Virtual Cell modeling has run into problems that have dampened excitement about systems biology.

items.excerpt:
💻 Code | 📊 Data | 🤖 Models | 📖 Documentation
Robots are learning to fold laundry, sort parts, and handle unfamiliar objects. But those demonstrations are often rather narrow and don't explain what a robot has learned or why it fails.
To study a complex system, scientists often begin with a small, controlled environment, such as a petri dish or terrarium, where they can vary conditions and observe the effects. Robotics needs environments that make this kind of investigation possible—researchers should be able to change the training data or model design, repeat a test, and trace the cause of a failure.
Today we're introducing a framework for creating these environments; we call them FoundationWorlds. Each pairs a controlled, simulated world targeted at studying robotics in a specific environment with tools for automatically generating tasks and training demonstrations, as well as metrics for measuring a robot's behavior over time. Together, they provide a setting for studying questions such as how models improve as more training data becomes available, and how to best combine high-level reasoning with precise physical control.
Our first foundation world is ToyBlocks : an open simulation framework built around a robot arm and blocks on a tabletop. The setting is deliberately simple, but the robot must still reason about how the blocks interact and how to arrange them while pushing, flipping, and stacking.

items.title: METR 审计称 Anthropic 可能早在 7 月已触发其自身 AI 加速预警阈值
items.description: METR 发布对 Anthropic 内部数据的十一周审计结果，称自 2025 年 10 月以来模型测试分数提升速度约加快 1.9 倍，其中约 80% 归因于 AI 用于公司自身研究，可能已在 7 月 15 日达到其负责任扩展政策中的预警阈值。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/vpopkx98s6mpp9coxhi7hhvh2
items.excerpt:
METR finds Anthropic may have crossed its own AI acceleration warning threshold back in July
METR 发布对 Anthropic 内部数据的十一周审计结果，称自 2025 年 10 月以来模型测试分数提升速度约加快 1.9 倍，其中约 80% 归因于 AI 用于公司自身研究，可能已在 7 月 15 日达到其负责任扩展政策中的预警阈值。
原文给出了 METR 审计的核心数字和被删除证据等细节，读者可以据此了解 Anthropic 自身加速预警阈值的争议。
非营利组织METR获得了为期十一周的权限，得以接触Anthropic的内部研究数据。其结论是：Anthropic模型的提升速度大约翻了一倍，而其中约80%的加速可追溯到AI被用于公司自身的研究。不过，Anthropic对最重要的证据做了涂黑处理。
AI是否正在加速更优AI的开发，被视为安全讨论中的一个关键早期预警信号。人们担心会形成一种反馈回路：模型越来越快地改进自己的后继者，而据 METR 称，这可能导致“极端且危险的能力突然涌现”。Anthropic在其 负责任扩展政策 中正是把这类加速列为风险指标：如果AI的进步速度因自动化AI研究而翻倍，就应触发警告级别。
这正是METR想要验证的。这家非营利组织研究的课题之一，是AI开发者是否可能失去对自家系统的控制。2026年8月12日至10月29日，一支相当于2.5名全职人员的团队获得了他们所称的“前所未有的权限”，可以查看未发布模型的基准测试结果、训练指标、员工调查和内部分析，并对Anthropic的研究人员进行了约15次访谈。METR没有收取Anthropic的任何费用，但出于安全考虑，工作是在Anthropic的设备上进行的。
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei此前曾 承诺引入外部审计方进入公司 。随后在10月，Anthropic 宣布与METR合作，给予其“类似员工的访问权限” 。据METR称，本次审计是另一个独立项目，范围更窄。
据METR称，自2025年10月以来，Anthropic模型测试分数的攀升速度约为2024年3月至2025年10月期间的1.9倍。这一衡量基于AECI，一个将多项基准测试打包在一起的综合指标。Anthropic用一年时间取得了此前需要两年才能实现的进展，大致相当于从Claude 2.1到Sonnet 4.5的跃升。分析还纳入了三个于2026年7月至10月间完成训练的未发布模型。2025年10月之前，Anthropic的模型每年约提升15个AECI点；此后，这一速度达到了29。
METR确信，这一加速并非由训练算力增长加快所驱动。相反，审计人员估计，当前约80%的提速来自AI被用于Anthropic自身的研究。一位员工在访谈中说：“现在瓶颈只在想法和算力上，不再卡在代码上了。”
还有人表示，过去需要一到两天才能搭好的实验，现在“几乎零成本”。在2026年10月的非正式Slack投票中，员工平均表示最新的内部模型让他们的效率提高了约十二倍。METR将这些自我评估视为“非常宽松的证据”，称其不具代表性，且很可能高估了实际收益。
目前 AI 还做不到完全自主研究。加速主要来自 AI 充当助手，但已经出现“生命迹象”，独立贡献可能很快发挥更大作用。METR 没有发现会在未来十二个月拖慢节奏的瓶颈，这意味着加速在未来一年继续扩大的“风险很大”。
METR 也强调结果有多不精确。真实的加速系数可能低至 1.3，也可能高达 3。把 OpenAI、Google 和 xAI 的模型算进来后，全行业的数字降到只有 1.4，可能是因为 Anthropic 在 2025 年落后于竞争对手，追赶效应扭曲了数据。
Anthropic 内部的观点也不统一。一位研究员认为 AI 在生产力提升中的贡献只占 15% 到 20%，并且不信任同事的自我报告。另一位则认为新员工是近几个月最重要的单一因素。
Anthropic 对所有非公开信息拥有单方面的删减权，并且大量行使了这一权利。据 METR 称，审计人员评为信息量最大的证据大部分被删掉了，包括对未来模型的预测、按训练步骤的细分以及瓶颈分析。Anthropic 称这些删减“旨在移除可能加速其他 AI 开发者的机密信息”。
结果是，公众不得不“远比理想情况更依赖”METR 的判断，该组织写道，而围绕证据的任何透明度讨论都无从谈起。METR 报告中有一张图相应地用大字标着“FAKE DATA”（假数据）。
在另一份 评审 中，METR 还审视了 Anthropic 2026 年 8 月的风险报告 。在那份报告里，公司公开表示加速“不到 2 倍”。但内部未删减版本暗示数值为 1.97，而 Anthropic 自己也称阈值被突破是“有可能的”。METR 认为警告级别可能在 7 月 15 日就已经达到，并指责公开报告既低估了加速程度，也低估了围绕它的不确定性。
METR 目前认同 Anthropic 的评估，即急性灾难性风险“低”，但该组织无法排除未来六个月再次出现急剧加速的可能，那可能很快把风险评级推高。
METR 原本还应该核实 Anthropic 如何在能力研究与安全研究之间分配算力。Anthropic 在项目进行到一半时取消了这部分，称想先专注于风险评估，之后再重新审视算力审计。
“AI 2027”情景背后的研究员 Daniel Kokotajlo 在 X 上 尖锐回应 ，认为审计算力分配正是让 放缓承诺 能够被验证的基础。

items.excerpt:
If you walk into a large, modern warehouse in North America, you would see technology everywhere, from mobile robots and conveyors to automated storage and more. All of it would be managed by a stack of integrated warehouse management systems that track every SKU and every order in real time. But if you took a few more steps out into the yard, that picture would change completely.
There’s a line of trucks waiting to be processed at the gate. Idle drivers sit in the yard while their engines and hours-of-service clocks continue to run.
Full trailers wait to be spotted. Empty trailers wait to be filled . And no one knows when the reefer units were last checked. There is chaos in every direction.
Even within relatively modern supply chain organizations, a significant sophistication gap persists between the warehouse and the yard.
Because the yard represents a small portion of a company’s total logistics spend, most operators manage the yard as an afterthought. It has not received anywhere near the same level of investment as workflows inside the four walls.
A picker inside a facility with a warehouse management system ( WMS ) knows exactly which item to retrieve next and where to find it. Without a similar yard operating system, a hostler doesn’t know which trailer to move next, let alone where to go and look for it.
Every day, one of the most sophisticated parts of a supply chain operation interfaces with people using clipboards and radios, creating inefficiencies and a lack of visibility.
The yard needs to be digitized . Despite its relatively small size, the yard has an outsized impact on supply chain performance inside the four walls. items.description: AI is thinning the entry-level supply chain workforce faster than the talent pipeline can be redesigned says Gartner.
items.excerpt:
In what many have feared, the impact of AI is taking a toll on headcount. A new Gartner survey shows that nearly half of supply chains have reduced headcount by an average of 10.5% over the past two years.
Additionally, 66% of supply chain leaders report headcount reduction is concentrated at the entry level, more than double the percentage reporting reduction at other levels in the supply chain workforce.
“AI is thinning the entry-level supply chain workforce faster than most chief supply chain officers (CSCOs) are redesigning the talent pipeline, creating a future capability gap that will actually weaken their organizations’ AI performance,” said Tess Frenzel, director analyst in Gartner's suppy chain practice, in a statement.
“While impacts to entry-level positions from AI continue to grab the most attention, our research also shows a notable change in expectations for the skills required for middle-management positions, compared with just two years ago,” Frenzel continued. “Producing fewer candidates for traditionally defined leadership roles is a miscalculation, as supply chains will require new competencies both for entry-level and leadership positions as a result of working alongside AI.”
Reducing entry-level hiring without meaningfully changing role responsibilities and requirements can create a more fragile talent pipeline. Supply chain organizations have traditionally relied on large entry-level workforces to produce qualified candidates for more senior positions, even amid high attrition. A smaller incoming workforce leaves fewer employees available to advance, increasing the importance of selecting, developing and retaining high-potential entry-level talent as leadership roles continue to evolve.
Additional analysis of the survey data found that high-performing supply chains, defined as the top 25% based on AI integration, AI-enabled automation, and business outcomes, are responding by elevating entry-level roles.
“Compared with two years ago, these organizations require more domain-specific and analytics skills and greater supply chain experience, while involving entry-level employees in less repetitive work and more consequential decisions,” said Frenzel. “This approach can attract and engage higher-skilled talent while better preparing employees to advance into the senior positions which will also evolve as AI is embedded within the organization.”

主动聚焦让 Muse 即使遇到意外挑战，也能继续朝着目标推进。我们针对现实世界中各种典型的瓶颈对模型进行了训练，使它们能更努力尝试、从挫折中恢复，或代你寻找替代方案。在 Muse 中，我们的模型在完成那些会出现意外问题的日常任务时，表现提升了 67%。
我们还开发了专用模型，让它们发挥 Muse Wonder 在 Muse 尤为看重的一些行为上的表现。例如，它们学会了成为出色的多任务处理者，知道何时独立推进你的目标，何时与你实时协作。它们还能在任务执行过程中更好地适应你的引导和澄清，而不会陷入混乱。
在 Meta AI 中，同样的改进让它成为更好的思考伙伴和协作者。它能把复杂问题拆解成清晰的步骤，提出更精准的追问，并在对话中途你改变方向时跟上节奏。
通过将上述专用模型加入 Muse 和 Meta AI ，我们希望让更多人用上能力更强的超级智能。我们期待你亲自体验。
